actions.action: Check the base of the stems for brown, thread-like rot (damping off)
Replant quickly in light, moist potting soil, burying the stem up to the first leaves
Water gently at the base to settle the soil
Afterwards, water only when the top of the soil is dry to the touch
Place in bright shade without direct sun for 2-3 days
Cover with a cut plastic bottle or clear bag to keep humidity
Air out the cover once a day
Then move to the sunniest window
Alternatively, use a grow lamp 12-14 hours a day
Plan B: keep stems that don't recover in a glass of water, changing the water every 2 days
Repot water-rooted stems once the roots reach 2-3 cm

reason: The answer correctly identifies transplant shock, but its main advice is replanting in soil, with keeping the stems in water (the actual fix) only a Plan B; nothing it suggests is likely to harm the plant.
